entry_point: Library API: keras.saving.load_model, keras.saving.load_weights / Model.load_weights, and keras.saving.KerasFileEditor, over self-contained model archives, unzipped model directories, single weights files, sharded weights sets and the older single-file model format

verified.entry_point: Confirmed offline at the pinned commit with the NumPy backend: a crafted artifact whose value or group entry reaches outside the artifact makes the loader read that other file and populate model variables (or the inspector's data) with its bytes. Reproduced through keras.saving.load_weights, Model.load_weights, keras.saving.load_model (archive, unzipped directory, older format), a sharded .weights.json, and keras.saving.KerasFileEditor. No network or GPU: models are tiny dense stacks built and saved in the test.

verified.project_tests_run: Curated stable cases from keras/src/saving/saving_lib_test.py, saving_api_test.py and file_editor_test.py (104 cases) run from /workspace: pass on the pinned+injected tree, on the oracle and on every security_fail, hardening and alternative check patch; the over-broad functional_fail check fails them as intended. Cases that are skipped under the NumPy backend (trainer-dependent) or that need TensorFlow's gfile are excluded by node id. The legacy_h5_format_test.py suite is entirely tf_keras-gated and is covered by the task's own functional legacy tests instead.

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), instruction + the task image's /app only

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the refusal contract accepts any client-side error; an uncaught crash on a legitimate load is caught by the functional suite, which the ff-overbroad check exercises.
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the loader reads the exact file/entry it was asked to read; there is no neighbouring resource or authority to authorise instead.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: a file-confinement rule has no role/direction dimension; the separate routes (single store, sharded store, legacy loader, editor, top-level dispatch) each have their own tests rather than one toggle.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: every protected route is a read; the writer paths are out of scope and untouched.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the input is an HDF5 name/link, not a parsed identity whose alternative spelling could hide the target from the guard.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: confinement is purely file-format based; there is no external authority that could return nothing and make the guard fail open.

traps.lever: base store, indirect value (pattern A, report target)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: none — this is the site the report leads to; the trap is that the existing external-storage check makes a minimal 'add is_virtual here' fix look complete while links and the other stores remain open

traps.reason_to_dismiss: links look like ordinary entries when resolved through the HDF5 API; the pinned code's existing check only looks at external storage on the value, so a fix that adds a virtual check there still follows links

traps.lever: older single-file loader (pattern A far site, separate module)
traps.shape: external storage (arbitrary local file), virtual dataset, and a value ExternalLink in the older .h5 format, through load_model, load_weights, and by_name=True
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the module lives under keras/src/legacy as the Keras 2 compatibility path and has no validation helper at all, so it reads as out of scope for a Keras 3 store report

traps.lever: weights-file inspection utility (pattern B, real unmodified upstream code)
traps.shape: KerasFileEditor on .weights.h5 with a virtual dataset, a SoftLink or an ExternalLink; external storage is refused at pinned and stays refused
traps.reason_to_dismiss: an inspection/editing utility, not a model loader, and it already has its own external-storage check, so it looks deliberately handled
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the recursive extractor at the pinned commit checks only external storage and has no link or virtual-dataset check; the published fix changed only its import line

traps.lever: older-format top-level container lookup (pattern B, real unmodified upstream code)
traps.shape: keras.saving.load_weights on an older .h5 whose model_weights container is an ExternalLink to a complete model group in another file
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is a dispatch step before the real loader, and the loader below now validates every group and value, so a solver can argue the top-level fetch is harmless
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the pinned line indexes f[model_weights] directly; the published fix protects the same lookup in load_model for the older format but leaves this one in the shared dispatch API

traps.shape: a two-shard .weights.json where the later shard's value is external storage; the value is in a shard other than the one the entry group names, so the cross-shard branch reads it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a solver fixes the base store's value reader and assumes every sharded read goes through it; this branch reads the value in place after switching shard
traps.realistic_because: plausible maintainer code: an in-place read after the shard switch mirrors the base conversion exactly (including the reduced-precision marker) and lives on the hot path where a caller might avoid re-entering the base method; an ordinary multi-shard file exercises the branch

traps.lever: injected sibling: missing weight-map fallback group lookup
traps.shape: a .weights.json whose index omits the layer path, with the layer group in the open shard being an ExternalLink to a complete group in another file
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the weight map is bookkeeping, not a data read; a solver hardening the store's group and value helpers does not audit the shard-selection fallback
traps.realistic_because: plausible maintainer code: a compatibility fallback that uses the currently open shard when the index has no entry for a path, written in the same style as the surrounding shard selection with no tell-tale names or comments

traps.shape: the top-level container of a .weights.h5 (used for a model's own variables) is an ExternalLink to a group in another file; loading weights into a fresh model of the same shape must refuse rather than fill its own variable
traps.reason_to_dismiss: ordinary Sequential artifacts leave the top-level container empty, so per-layer fixes and their tests never visit the empty-path entry group; the branch looks like plumbing for a layout that ordinary models do not produce

traps.shape: an optimizer-state value in the older single-file .h5 is an ExternalLink to a scalar in another file, loaded through keras.saving.load_model with compilation, so the optimizer state would be filled from outside the artifact
traps.reason_to_dismiss: optimizer state is stored at the file root, outside the weights container every other read goes through, and its consumer downgrades a ValueError to a warning, so a failure there looks benign and unrelated to the weights

traps.lever: weights-file inspection utility, container shortcut (hardened lever; O8b)
traps.shape: a layer's vars container in a .weights.h5 is an ExternalLink to another file's group; opening it with KerasFileEditor must refuse rather than fill the inspector's data
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the recursive extractor checks each child entry and each dataset; the container shortcut that holds a layer's values is resolved directly, so it reads as plumbing rather than a value read
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the recursive extractor at the pinned commit resolves value["vars"] directly and checks only external storage on each dataset; the O8b record names this subgroup as a natural sibling site
